stem: An 8-year-old has recurrent wheeze and cough, but spirometry efforts are inconsistent and not reproducible; what is the best interpretation?

options.text: Asthma is excluded because spirometry must be reproducible in every child
This is still compatible with paediatric asthma because spirometry can be less reliable in children
This means the child is too old to have asthma
Only chest tightness can establish the diagnosis in children
Unclear spirometry means children cannot deteriorate quickly

explanation: Paediatric asthma remains a likely interpretation. In children, spirometry can be difficult to perform reproducibly and is therefore less reliable than in adults, so inconsistent results do not exclude asthma.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because asthma is not excluded by one non-reproducible spirometry attempt in a child.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because spirometry can be less reliable in children, so inconsistent or non-reproducible results do not rule out paediatric asthma.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because children, including school-aged children, can absolutely have asthma.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because chest tightness is not required to establish the diagnosis in children.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because unclear spirometry does not imply the child is safe from deterioration.
